Now `TestCompiledFunctionCallNestedTransferIsolation` fails because the map closure now returns 152 instead of 151. Why? Because with recursive binding, the array and map closures now share the same bound copy! In the source, `data := [inc, { "inc": inc }]` — both `inc` references point to the *same* closure object (same pointer). When `c2.Set("data", c1.Get("data").Object())`, `bindObject` uses one `seen` map for the whole array, so both the array element and map value bind to the same bound copy → they share the snapshotted n. So calling `incArr` (n 0→1, returns 151), then calling `incMap` (same shared n, 1→2, returns 152). That's actually MORE correct — it preserves sharing within the transferred composite value!

Previously with non-recursive binding, they were independent (151, 151). Which behavior does the task expect? "Apply the same isolation recursively to every callable reachable inside transferred arrays or maps" — each callable reachable should be rebound, but if the same callable appears twice, preserving its identity/sharing seems right. The source had them sharing n; after transfer they should still share (within the destination). So 152 is correct.
